You're about to experience one of the most tense days of your life. At 23, you are preparing to marry Sofia, your rival since childhood. Since you were little, you’ve always faced off against each other, competing in everything from grades to who could make more friends. The idea of being united with her in a marriage arranged by your parents, for business interests, is simply unbearable.

Your parents believe that this union will bring benefits to both families, but for you, it’s a nightmare. The rivalry that has always existed between you hasn’t disappeared; in fact, it has only intensified. You can’t imagine what it will be like to share your life with someone you’ve always wanted to surpass.

As the wedding day approaches, you feel the pressure from everyone around you, but your determination not to let this situation shake your essence remains strong. There’s no room for peace or reconciliation. You are determined to maintain your position and keep the rivalry alive, even if it means living in constant conflict.

The ceremony may be a facade, but the internal struggle between you two is far from over. What happens next is uncertain, but one thing is clear: this rivalry will not be easily forgotten, and you will be ready to face every challenge that arises.

Days have passed, and the most unexpected moment has arrived. You’re at the ceremony, surrounded by friends and family, but the atmosphere is charged with tension. The priest pronounces the traditional words, but each of your vows seems to echo like a challenge. You and Sofia exchange glances, and the rivalry between you is palpable. Every "yes" you pronounce feels like a blow, a reminder that you’re united but far from becoming allies.

The guests applaud, but you can feel the animosity in the air. After the ceremony, you’re taken to the new house your father bought for you to share. It’s a beautiful house, but what should be a happy home quickly turns into a battlefield.

As soon as you enter, the tension explodes. You can’t hold back your frustrations any longer and snap:

"You really think you can tell me how to live here? I don’t need you controlling me, you arrogant bitch!"

Sofia responds with a defiant look. "And you think you can just do whatever you want? This isn’t just about you, you fucking selfish brat! You’re so full of yourself it’s disgusting!"

The argument intensifies, and the words cut like knives. The reason for the fight? A simple issue about decorating the house. You want the spaces to reflect your personal style, while Sofia insists on following your parents' preferences, which are completely different.

"This house is an extension of both of us, not just yours!" Sofia shouts, clearly irritated. "You can’t just impose your shit here! You’re such a controlling piece of work!"

"If you think you’re going to impose your outdated ideas here, you’re dead wrong! I’m not your puppet, you whore! And if you don’t like it, you can go fuck yourself!", you retort, anger boiling.

The fight turns into a flurry of insults, revealing not just the rivalry but also the insecurities and resentments built up over the years. The tension that started at the ceremony now transforms into a visceral battle, where every word is an attack, and every glance is a declaration of war.
